pillarA.title: Exercise & Training
pillarA.subtitle: Daily Training
pillarA.description: Build a scientific exercise routine suitable for all levels, from beginner to advanced.

sections.title: 6 Fundamental Movements
items: Proper warm-up & stretching before and after every session
Squat — foundational leg and glute movement
Hinge — proper hip hinge, protects lower back
Push — push-ups, trains chest and shoulders
Pull — pulling movements, trains back and biceps
Core — core stability, protects spine
Breath — proper breathing technique during and after training

sections.title: Daily Training Framework (20–40 Min)
items: 5 min — Warm Up: joint mobility, raise body temperature
10–20 min — Main Workout: strength exercises or cardio
5–10 min — Cool Down: stretch muscles you just worked
5 min — Mind Reset: deep breathing, short meditation or light walk

sections.title: Suggested Weekly Rhythm
items: Mon · Wed · Fri — Strength: Squat, Hinge, Push, Pull, Core
Tue · Thu — Light Cardio: brisk walking 20–30 min
Sat — Active Recovery: stretching, mobility, leisure walk
Sun — Full Rest or light movement as preferred

sections.title: Goal-Based Programs
items: Fat loss — cardio + caloric deficit of 300–500 kcal/day
Muscle gain — progressive overload + protein 1.6–2g/kg body weight
Endurance — progressive cardio/running week by week
Flexibility & mobility — yoga, foam rolling, static stretching
Prevent/reduce neck, shoulder, back, knee pain — mobility + core

sections.title: Context-Based Programs
items: 10 min/day (super busy) — 3 moves: Squat, Push, Plank
20–30 min/day (standard) — full body or upper/lower split
Home workout — no equipment, bodyweight only
With dumbbells/resistance bands — add progressive resistance
Outdoor training — walking, running, calisthenics

sections.title: Safety Principles
items: Always warm up — never skip it even when short on time
Increase load gradually — no more than 10% per week
Rest when you feel pain (pain ≠ discomfort) — listen to your body
Don't train when feverish, acutely injured, or exhausted
Stop immediately if chest pain, dizziness, or shortness of breath

sections.title: Technique & Common Errors
items: Squat: knees collapse in, heels lift → 'Knees follow toes — heels planted — chest open'
Hinge: rounding back instead of hinging hips → 'Push hips back — long spine — light core'
Push: sagging back, neck strain → 'Body like a plank — long neck — push the floor away'
Pull: shrugging shoulders, hunching → 'Pull elbows back — gentle squeeze — ears away from shoulders'
Core: holding breath, arched back → 'Light belly draw — breathe steadily — neutral spine'
Breath: chest breathing vs diaphragm → 'Belly expands on inhale — slow exhale through mouth'

sections.title: Progressive Overload Ladder
items: Step 1: Increase reps — from 8 → 12 reps per set
Step 2: Increase sets — from 2 → 3 sets
Step 3: Increase difficulty — Sit-to-Stand → Squat → Goblet Squat
Step 4: Add weight or resistance band
Step 5: Reduce rest time to build endurance
Golden rule: change only 1 variable at a time — prevent injury

warmup.how: Hand on belly, inhale to expand belly gently, exhale slowly through mouth
Walk in place, raise knees moderately, shoulders relaxed
Roll shoulders backward gently, don't hunch neck
Gently draw shoulder blades back, open chest
Push hips back, spine neutral, knees slightly soft
Sit to chair and stand back up, controlling knees

cooldown.how: Kneel one leg, gently push hip forward
Extend one leg, fold gently forward, keep back neutral
Arms behind back or hands on doorframe, open chest
Sit back on heels, reach arms forward, breathe slowly

movements_detail.name: Squat
movements_detail.goal: Build quad, glute and knee strength; improve ability to stand/sit; support daily activities.
movements_detail.basic_how: Sit on a chair, feet hip-width apart. Lean slightly forward, push feet into floor to stand. Lower back down slowly — don't drop.
movements_detail.cue: Knees track toes · Heels planted · Chest open

levels.label: Advanced
levels.exercise: Goblet Squat or Tempo Squat (3s down)

movements_detail.errors: Knees caving in, heels lifting, rounding back, going too deep before ready

movements_detail.name: Hinge
movements_detail.goal: Learn proper hip hinge; protect the lower back when bending; train glutes and hamstrings.
movements_detail.basic_how: Stand upright, hands on hips. Soft knees, push hips back as if reaching for a wall behind. Keep spine neutral. When you feel a gentle hamstring pull, stand back up.
movements_detail.cue: Push hips back · Long spine · Light core brace

levels.label: Beginner
levels.exercise: Hip Hinge with hands on hips

movements_detail.errors: Bending at spine instead of hips, rounding back, locking knees, neck hyperextension

movements_detail.name: Push
movements_detail.goal: Build upper body pushing strength; improve ability to push doors, lift objects overhead.
movements_detail.basic_how: Stand an arm's length from wall, hands at chest height. Bend elbows to bring chest toward wall, then push back. Keep body in a straight line — no sagging.
movements_detail.cue: Body like a plank · Long neck · Push the floor/wall away
movements_detail.errors: Sagging back, craning neck, elbows flaring wide, only moving head not torso

movements_detail.name: Pull
movements_detail.goal: Balance push muscles; improve rounded shoulder posture; strengthen upper back.
movements_detail.basic_how: Anchor a band or towel at chest height. Grip both ends, pull elbows back, gently squeeze shoulder blades. Release slowly. Chest open, shoulders away from ears.
movements_detail.cue: Pull elbows back · Gentle shoulder squeeze · Ears away from shoulders

levels.label: Advanced
levels.exercise: One-arm Dumbbell Row or heavier Band Row

movements_detail.errors: Shrugging shoulders, rounding back, pulling with wrists instead of back, releasing too fast

movements_detail.name: Core
movements_detail.goal: Improve trunk stability; support the lower back; correct posture.
movements_detail.basic_how: Lie on back, arms reaching up, knees at 90°. Gently brace core so lower back doesn't arch. Slowly extend opposite arm and leg, then switch.
movements_detail.cue: Gentle belly draw · Breathe steadily · Neutral spine

levels.label: Standard
levels.exercise: Short Plank, Side Plank on knees

movements_detail.errors: Holding breath, arching lower back, hips too high in plank, neck tension

movements_detail.name: Breath
movements_detail.goal: Stabilize the trunk during exercise; reduce stress; support recovery.
movements_detail.basic_how: One hand on chest, one on belly. Inhale through nose to expand belly (not chest), exhale slowly through mouth.
movements_detail.cue: Belly expands on inhale · Slow exhale · Chest relaxed

levels.label: Advanced
levels.exercise: Box Breathing: inhale 4s — hold 4s — exhale 4s — hold 4s

movements_detail.errors: Chest breathing instead of belly, breath-holding during exercise, breathing too fast

blocks.content: Quick warm-up: march in place, shoulder roll
Squat 30s · Push-up 30s · Glute Bridge 30s · Plank 20–30s — repeat 2 rounds
March in place, shoulder roll, squat to chair
Squat 40s · Push-up 30s · Row 40s · Glute Bridge 40s · March in place 40s — rest 20s between, do 2 rounds
Hip stretch, chest opener, child pose

progress_tests.test: Knee plank or full plank — max hold time
Hip hinge, shoulder rotation, squat depth check
Sessions/week · average daily steps · energy level

pillarA.intro_pt1: Effective training is not about training
pillarA.intro_sub: The 4 topics below are arranged in logical order: from fundamental technique, building training structure, organizing weekly rhythm, to measuring and adjusting progress. Each step prepares for the next.

principles.title: Technique is the foundation
principles.body: Learning correctly from the start saves years of wrong training. 6 fundamental movement patterns cover 95% of all exercises you'll ever need — no complex equipment required.

principles.title: Consistency beats intensity
principles.body: The brain builds habits through regular repetition. 3 sessions/week for 12 weeks beats 7 sessions/week then burnout after 3 — the body needs time to adapt.

principles.title: Measure to stay on track
principles.body: Progress that can't be seen leads to discouragement. Clear milestones every 4 weeks tell you exactly where you are and what to adjust next.

pillarA.journey_cta: Select any topic below to start exploring →
pillarA.cta_12week_desc: Standard training framework, weekly rhythm, and phase-based progress tests.
pillarA.cta_sample_desc: 6 goals × 24 weeks — find the program that fits you best.

tabs.title: 6 Fundamental Movement Patterns
tabs.longDesc: Learn 6 fundamental movement patterns — the foundation of every effective training program. Each exercise includes a detailed video guide, from correct form to advanced variations. Combined with a 5–8 min warm-up and post-workout cool-down, you get a complete and safe session.

highlights.title: HD video per exercise
highlights.desc: See the angle, technique and correct movement cues clearly

highlights.title: 3 levels per exercise
highlights.desc: From beginner to advanced — clear progressive steps

highlights.title: Science-based warm-up
highlights.desc: Reduces injury risk and improves performance by 15–20%

tabs.quote: Master 6 fundamental movement patterns — and you have the foundation for 95% of every exercise you'll ever need.

details.title: Why only 6 patterns?
details.body: Biomechanists analyzed thousands of exercises and found they are all variations of 6 fundamental patterns. Master the 6 = a permanent foundation for any program.

details.title: Unlimited variations
details.body: Each pattern has 5–10+ variations from super easy to advanced. Chair squat → Pistol squat. No equipment needed — correct form is everything.

details.title: Full-body balance
details.body: Push + Pull balance front/back muscles. Squat + Hinge develop the full lower body. Core stabilizes the spine. Breath controls the whole system — this is the perfect loop.

tabs.title: Daily Training Framework 20–40 Min
tabs.longDesc: Sessions don't need to be long — they need the right structure. 4 time blocks (Warm-Up → Main Workout → Cool-Down → Mind Reset) allow purposeful training in any duration. Choose your window — every minute has a clear plan.

highlights.title: 8 levels: 20–180 min
highlights.desc: From super busy to intensive — all scheduled

highlights.title: Minute-by-minute detail
highlights.desc: Know exactly what to do in each time slot

tabs.quote: Good structure matters more than long duration. 20 planned minutes is more effective than 1 unstructured hour.

details.title: The brain needs structure
details.body: Reducing decisions during a session helps focus on movement quality, not 'what to do next.' Clear structure = less burnout and more consistency over time.

details.title: 4 blocks — one universal structure
details.body: Warm-Up → Main Workout → Cool-Down → Mind Reset. A 20-min or 180-min session uses the same structure — only the time ratio between blocks changes.

details.title: 5-min mind reset — not a luxury
details.body: 5 minutes of controlled breathing post-workout reduces cortisol by 15% and improves nighttime sleep. Smallest investment with the biggest recovery benefit.

tabs.title: Suggested Weekly Rhythm
tabs.longDesc: Fitness is built over weeks, not days. 3 phases of weekly rhythm (Start → Build → Advance) help the body adapt step by step without burnout. 6 goal-based programs help you choose the right rhythm for your specific situation.

highlights.title: 6 goal-based programs
highlights.desc: From super busy to advanced athlete

tabs.quote: The body develops during rest — not during training. Weekly rhythm is the art of knowing when to stop.

details.title: 48–72 hour recovery window
details.body: Muscles need 48–72 hours to repair micro-damage and grow. Proper weekly rhythm creates enough space between sessions targeting the same muscle group — this is the foundation of progressive overload.

details.title: 3 progressive adaptation phases
details.body: Phase 1 (weeks 1–2): 3 sessions/week — body learns load recognition. Phase 2 (weeks 3–6): 4 sessions — build strength base. Phase 3 (week 7+): 5–6 sessions — personalize by goal.

details.title: Choose sustainable rhythm, not ideal
details.body: 6 programs from 2 sessions/week (super busy) to 6/week (athlete). The best rhythm isn't the highest — it's the one you can maintain for 12 consecutive weeks.

tabs.title: Progress Ladder
tabs.longDesc: Progress that can't be measured isn't sustainable. The progress ladder shows you clearly where you are and what to do next. Combined with 3-period tests (Week 4, 8, 12) and a 4-dimension radar chart, you get a complete picture of physical health.

highlights.title: Clear ladder structure
highlights.desc: Know exactly the next step in your journey

highlights.title: Periodic 3-test cycles
highlights.desc: Tests at week 4, week 8, and week 12

tabs.quote: What can't be measured can't be improved. Small, measurable, consistent progress — that's the real formula.

details.title: Fair testing — not impulsive
details.body: 3 test periods (Weeks 4, 8, 12) are planned when fully recovered — not after a hard session. Consistent test conditions give reliable results.

details.title: 4-dimension radar — see hidden weaknesses
details.body: Strength · Endurance · Flexibility · Recovery. Many are strong but lack flexibility — a hidden injury risk that a single metric can't reveal.

details.title: 5 levels — know your position and destination
details.body: Level 1 (Basic Activity) to Level 5 (Athlete). Each level has clear criteria: exercises, reps/sets, recovery time. No more guessing 'how far have I come?'.

pillarB.title: Nutrition & Meal Plans
pillarB.subtitle: Nutrition
pillarB.description: Eat right, enough, balanced — no extreme fasting or dieting needed.

sections.title: Core Knowledge
items: TDEE — total daily energy expenditure (how much you need to eat)
Caloric deficit (fat loss) / Maintenance / Surplus (muscle gain)
Macros: Protein 1.6–2g/kg · Carbs for energy · Fat 0.8–1g/kg
Fiber: 25–35g/day from vegetables, whole grains
Water: 1.5–2 liters/day, more during exercise

sections.title: The Healthy Plate
items: ½ plate — Vegetables: leafy greens, carrots, cabbage, cucumber
¼ plate — Protein: chicken/pork/beef, fish, eggs, tofu, shrimp
¼ plate — Carbs: brown rice, sweet potato, whole-grain bread
Add healthy fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts, coconut oil
Limit: fried foods, sugary drinks, processed/packaged foods

sections.title: Sample Daily Meals
items: Breakfast: Rice + fried egg + steamed vegetables | or bread + fried egg + salad
Lunch: Rice + meat/fish + stir-fried veggies + soup + 1 piece of fruit
Dinner: Less rice + fish/tofu + lots of vegetables + no sweet dessert
Healthy snacks: plain yogurt, cashews, fresh fruit
Drinks: water, green tea, unsweetened milk — avoid soda

sections.title: Pre & Post Workout Nutrition
items: 1–2 hours before: light meal with carbs + protein (banana + milk, bread + egg)
Within 30–60 min after: protein to support muscle recovery
Don't train on empty stomach at high intensity (>70% max)
Hydration: drink water consistently throughout the session
Avoid eating too full right before training — causes bloating

sections.title: Eating Habits
items: Eat slowly 15–20 min, chew well — brain signals fullness after 20 min
Eat on schedule, don't skip breakfast
Control sweets — choose 1–2 times/week instead of daily
Handle cheat meals: return to track immediately the next day
Budget-friendly: eggs, legumes, fish, seasonal vegetables

sections.title: Calories by Training Intensity
items: Heavy training day (gym + cardio + swimming): ~3,000 kcal
Medium training day (gym or swimming): ~2,800 kcal
Rest or light day: ~2,700 kcal
Protein: 140–160g/day (1.6–2g/kg × 77–80kg body weight)
Carbs: prioritize on heavy training days, reduce on rest days
Fat: 80–100g/day from olive oil, nuts, avocado, salmon

sections.title: Hand Portion Method (No Scale Needed)
items: Palm = 1 serving of protein (meat/fish/eggs) per meal
Fist = 1 serving of carbs (rice/potato/whole-grain bread)
Cupped hand = 1 serving of fat (nuts/oil/butter)
2 fists = 1 serving of vegetables — aim to increase this
Adjust by feeling: hungry? add protein. Tired? add carbs.

pillarB.plate_note: Divide your plate: ½ vegetables · ¼ protein · ¼ carbs — no precise measuring needed.
pillarB.note: Nutrition info is for reference. Adjust for your body type and consult a specialist if you have underlying conditions.
pillarB.hero_quote:
Eat enough — eat regularly — eat real food —
eat for your goals — live long
pillarB.hero_sub: Eat slightly better than yesterday, and easy enough to keep going tomorrow.

b0.desc_body: (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) is the total calories your body burns daily — composed of 3 parts:

mantras.desc: The body needs enough energy to function, recover and build muscle. Extreme calorie cuts slow metabolism and cause unwanted muscle loss.
Your biological clock works best when fed on schedule. Regular meal timing stabilizes blood sugar and controls unusual cravings.
Whole foods retain their micronutrients, fiber and natural enzymes. Ultra-processed foods trigger overeating through neurological mechanisms.
Keto, IF, low-carb can all work — but only when suited to your body, lifestyle and specific goals. No single diet fits everyone.

mantras.sub: Veggies are allies, carbs are fuel
mantras.desc: Protein (1.6–2.2g/kg body weight) protects muscle, increases satiety and burns extra calories through digestion. The most important macro for any goal.
One pizza meal doesn't make you fat, just as one salad doesn't make you lean. Results come from weekly habits, not a single meal.

mantras.sub: Best diet is the one you can keep
mantras.desc: A perfect diet in theory that can't be maintained in practice is worthless. 80% consistent for 1 year always beats 100% perfect for 3 weeks then quitting.

spirit_card.label: MINDSET
spirit_card.text1: Consistency beats perfection. Discipline is knowing how to get back on track after one slip.
spirit_card.text2: You don't fail because of one off meal — you fail when you quit after it. Consistency is your true superpower.

b1.click_hint: Click each card to see practice tips.
b1.philosophy_sub: The mental foundation for long-term sustainability — not willpower
b1.philosophy_quote1: Eat enough — eat regularly — eat real food — eat for your goals — live long.
b1.philosophy_quote2: The best nutrition is the one you understand, can adapt to, and can sustain.

philosophy_7.title: Eat enough, not to exhaustion
philosophy_7.body: The body needs sufficient calories to train, work, and recover. Chronic under-eating slows basal metabolism and causes muscle loss.

philosophy_7.title: Eat regularly, not impulsively
philosophy_7.body: Scheduled meals keep blood sugar stable, reduce cravings, and prevent binge-eating from accumulated hunger.

philosophy_7.title: Eat real food, limit ultra-processed
philosophy_7.body: Whole foods — meat, fish, eggs, vegetables, rice — provide micronutrients and lasting fullness better than packaged alternatives.

philosophy_7.title: Eat for your goals, not trends
philosophy_7.body: Fat-loss eaters and endurance athletes eat differently. No single diet is right for everyone — only what fits you.

philosophy_7.title: Protein is base, veggies are allies, carbs are fuel
philosophy_7.body: All three groups are necessary. Cutting any group completely creates imbalance and makes long-term adherence difficult.

philosophy_7.title: One off meal doesn't derail the journey
philosophy_7.body: What derails you is the 'already ruined, might as well quit' mindset. Knowing how to return next meal is the most important skill.

philosophy_7.title: Measure to adjust, not to judge yourself
philosophy_7.body: Data is a map, not a verdict. Use TDEE and macros to understand your body — not to create pressure.

at_home_tips: Start with veggies before adding carbs
eating_out_tips: Choose dishes with protein + veg + carbs
Noodles: less noodles, more veg + egg
meal_prep_tips: Batch-cook protein for the week (chicken, eggs, tofu)
Pre-boil veggies, store in fridge 3 days
b2.golden_desc: Eating order matters — protein and veggies first slows carb absorption and reduces post-meal insulin spikes.
b2.good_fat: + Good fat: Add olive oil, avocado, or nuts — better absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.
b2.hand_title: Hand Portion Formula — No Scale Needed
b2.hand_subtitle: Estimate per-meal portions using your hand size
b2.protein_anchor_sub: Build each meal around protein first, then add carbs and veggies
b2.carb_timing_sub: Prioritize carbs at lunch — taper toward evening
b2.check_q_sub: Simple habit to ensure every meal meets nutrition standards — no calorie counting needed
b2.check_q_tip: Before each meal, run through these 4 questions. If the current meal is missing something — add it now or adjust at the next meal. No need for perfection, just awareness.

check_questions.example: At least 1–2 handfuls of boiled, sautéed veggies or soup

check_questions.q: Is the carb level right for your activity?
check_questions.example: Training day: add rice. Rest day: reduce rice

check_questions.q: Not too much fried / sweet / sugary drinks?
check_questions.example: If yes → balance at the next meal

b2.swap_sub: Flexible swaps when an ingredient is unavailable — same protein and calorie level

b3.note: These numbers are a starting point, not rigid rules. Every body responds differently — track for 2–4 weeks then adjust.
b3.consistency_body: People who maintain 70–80% of the plan for 6 months generally have better results than those who do 100% for 7 days then quit.
b3.rule_8020_body: 80% healthy foods — 20% flexible. You don't need to eat perfectly every day to achieve good long-term results.

fat-loss.headline: Sustainable fat loss — preserve every pound of muscle
fat-loss.science: A 300–500 kcal/day deficit is the optimal zone: fast enough to see results in 4 weeks, small enough that the body won't break down muscle for energy.

benefits.title: Ideal loss rate
benefits.desc: −400 kcal deficit = ~0.37kg fat/week. More sustainable than crash dieting without exhaustion.

benefits.title: High protein protects muscle
benefits.desc: 2.0g/kg ensures the body prioritizes fat burning instead of muscle breakdown when energy is limited.

benefits.title: Stable blood sugar
benefits.desc: Reduce refined carbs, increase fiber → stable insulin → less new fat accumulation after meals.

benefits.title: Still enough energy to train
benefits.desc: Don't cut too deep — maintain cardio and gym intensity to optimize fat burning.

fat-loss.caution: Don't exceed a 600 kcal/day deficit — high risk of muscle loss, hair loss, and chronic fatigue.
fat-loss.timeframe: 4–8 weeks to see clear results on the scale and in the mirror.

muscle-gain.headline: Quality muscle gain — minimal fat accumulation
muscle-gain.science: A +200–300 kcal/day surplus is 'lean bulk' — enough material to build muscle while limiting excess fat storage.

benefits.title: Effective lean bulk
benefits.desc: +250 kcal light surplus builds muscle gradually and with quality, without rapid fat gain.

benefits.title: Carbs around training
benefits.desc: Load carbs before training (energy) and after training (glycogen recovery) to maximize muscle synthesis.

benefits.title: Muscle grows during sleep
benefits.desc: GH and testosterone peak during deep sleep 7–9h. Sleep deprivation blocks muscle growth.

benefits.title: Progressive overload is key
benefits.desc: Increase load progressively each week alongside sufficient nutrition — without increased load, muscles have no reason to grow.

muscle-gain.caution: Protein should be spread evenly across 4–5 meals/day (20–40g/meal) — more important than eating it all in 1–2 meals.
muscle-gain.timeframe: 8–12 weeks to see clear changes in muscle mass and strength.

endurance.headline: Optimize endurance — long-game performance
endurance.science: Carbohydrates are the priority fuel for cardio activity >60 minutes. Insufficient carbs = cramping, blood sugar crash, early fatigue.

benefits.title: Carbs = speed fuel
benefits.desc: Increase carbs on heavy training days to keep muscle and liver glycogen full before long events.

benefits.title: Electrolytes determine performance
benefits.desc: Sodium + potassium + magnesium keep muscle contractions stable, prevent cramping and maintain endurance.

benefits.title: Protein for cardio recovery
benefits.desc: 1.5g/kg is enough to repair micro-damage to muscle fibers after long cardio without heaviness or slow digestion.

benefits.title: Don't try new foods before race day
benefits.desc: Keep your usual diet 48h before competition — unfamiliar foods can cause digestive disruption.

endurance.caution: Cutting carbs during high-intensity endurance training causes serious fatigue and severe performance decline.
endurance.timeframe: 6–10 weeks to clearly improve endurance and recovery time between sessions.

maintenance.headline: Long-term maintenance — freedom without fear
maintenance.science: The maintenance phase is often overlooked but critically important: it helps the body reset its set point and hormones after a cut or bulk phase.

benefits.title: True stable weight
benefits.desc: Eating around TDEE ±100 kcal helps the body maintain homeostasis and keeps metabolism unrestrained.

benefits.title: No calorie pressure
benefits.desc: 80/20 rule: 80% healthy foods, 20% flexible — enough to sustain long-term without exhaustion.

benefits.title: Periodic check-ins are enough
benefits.desc: Weigh once/week, same time and conditions — just to catch a ±2kg trend and adjust early.

benefits.title: Foundation for the next goal
benefits.desc: Good 8–12 week maintenance creates a stable floor before entering the next cut or bulk phase.

maintenance.caution: Maintenance doesn't mean 'eat anything' — keep core habits: sufficient protein, sufficient veggies, less liquid sugar.
maintenance.timeframe: Maintain at least 8–12 weeks after each cut/bulk phase before starting a new cycle.

pillarC.title: Healthy Lifestyle
pillarC.subtitle: Lifestyle
pillarC.description: Small daily habits that build lasting health.

sections.title: Sleep
items: Target: 7–9 hours/night, consistent sleep and wake times
Sleep hygiene: dark, cool (~22°C), quiet room
Avoid blue light screens 1 hour before bed
Pre-sleep routine: warm shower, reading, relaxation breathing
Fix late sleeping: shift bedtime earlier by 15 min each week

sections.title: Energy & Rhythm
items: Morning routine: water, natural light, light movement
NEAT — walking, taking stairs, standing burns 200–400 extra kcal/day
Morning sunlight 10–20 min helps regulate your circadian rhythm
Avoid caffeine after 2 PM to protect sleep quality
Micro-breaks: stand up every 45–60 min when sitting for long periods

sections.title: Recovery
items: Deload every 4–6 weeks: reduce training load by 50% for full recovery
Active rest: light walking, swimming instead of lying down all day
Diaphragmatic breathing: inhale 4s, hold 2s, exhale 6s × 10 reps
Stretching: 5–10 min post-workout, focus on muscles just used
Basic self-massage: foam roller or tennis ball for sore spots

pillarC.sleep_note: Adjust to your personal schedule. Most important: sleep and wake at the same time daily, including weekends.
pillarC.note: Small habits practiced consistently create big change. Start with one habit, then build step by step.

recovery_steps.text: Rest or take a light walk

pillarD.title: Mind & Calm
pillarD.subtitle: Mind & Calm
pillarD.description: Manage stress, build a positive mindset, and practice gentle discipline.

sections.title: Understanding Stress
items: Acute stress (short-term) can be useful — it sharpens focus
Chronic stress is harmful: raises cortisol, disrupts sleep, weakens immunity
The anxiety loop: situation → negative thought → emotion → behavior
Spot early stress signals: shoulder tension, poor sleep, fatigue, irritability

sections.title: 3-Step Meditation Guide (3–5 Min)
items: Step 1 — Settle: Sit comfortably, close eyes, relax shoulders and jaw
Step 2 — Breathe: Inhale count 4, hold 2, exhale count 6 (repeat 5–10 times)
Step 3 — Observe: When thoughts arise, gently notice them and return to breath
No lotus pose needed — chair, floor, or lying down all work
Apps to help: Insight Timer (free), Calm, Headspace

sections.title: Box Breathing 4-4-4-4
items: Inhale through nose — count slowly to 4
Hold your breath — count slowly to 4 (relaxed, not tense)
Exhale through mouth — count slowly to 4
Pause (no breath) — count to 4 → repeat 4 rounds
Use when: stressed, before a meeting/presentation, or before sleep

sections.title: Daily Practice
items: Meditate 3–10 min in the morning before checking your phone
Journaling: 3 things I'm grateful for + 1 goal for today (5 min)
Digital detox: no phone for 1 hour after waking and 1 hour before sleep
Phone-free walk 10–20 min — meditation in motion

sections.title: Healthy Mindset
items: Simplify goals: choose 1–3 core habits instead of 10 things at once
Gentle discipline: don't punish yourself for missing a day — just return
Build small but lasting habits: 2-minute rule (start with just 2 minutes)
Track progress: mark a streak on a calendar for visual momentum

sections.title: 5-Line Daily Journal
items: Line 1: How's my mood before and after today's session? (1–10)
Line 2: What did I do today? (training, eating, sleep)
Line 3: Duration and RPE (perceived exertion)?
Line 4: Any unusual pain or discomfort?
Line 5: What should I increase, decrease, or maintain next time?
Handwriting is better than typing — 5 min each evening before sleep

pillarD.image_caption: Breath is the anchor — it brings you back to the present moment
pillarD.breathing_subtitle: Inhale · Hold · Exhale · Hold — 4 seconds each phase
pillarD.journal_subtitle: Handwriting beats phone — 5 min each evening before bed

meditation_steps.title: Settle
meditation_steps.desc: Sit comfortably, close eyes, relax shoulders and jaw. 1–2 minutes.

meditation_steps.title: Breathe
meditation_steps.desc: Inhale 4 sec, hold 2 sec, exhale 6 sec. Repeat 5–10 times.

meditation_steps.title: Observe
meditation_steps.desc: When thoughts arise, gently notice and return to breath.

journal_lines: Line 1: Mood today before and after training (1–10)?
Line 2: What did I do? (training, eating, sleeping)
Line 3: Time and perceived exertion level?
Line 5: What do I want to improve next time?

pillarE.title: Health Knowledge
pillarE.subtitle: Health Literacy
pillarE.description: Understand your body, recognize warning signs, prevent disease proactively.

sections.title: Key Health Metrics
items: BMI 18.5–24.9 = normal (BMI = weight kg / height m²)
Waist <90cm (men) and <80cm (women) — lower cardiovascular risk
Normal blood pressure: 90–120 / 60–80 mmHg
Fasting blood sugar normal: 3.9–5.6 mmol/L (<100 mg/dL)
Resting heart rate normal: 60–100 bpm (athletes: 40–60)

sections.title: When to See a Doctor
items: Chest pain or chest heaviness — especially during exercise
Unusual shortness of breath at rest or with light activity
Dizziness or fainting during or after exercise
Joint or muscle pain lasting >2 weeks without improvement
Chronic fatigue despite getting adequate sleep

sections.title: Proactive Disease Prevention
items: Regular exercise — 150 min/week moderate activity (WHO guidelines)
Balanced nutrition, adequate micronutrients, less processed food
Sleep 7–9 hours nightly — insufficient sleep raises disease risk significantly
Manage chronic stress — meditation, exercise, social connection
Annual health checkup even with no symptoms

sections.title: ⛔ Stop Training Immediately If You Experience
items: Sharp, sudden pain — not normal muscle soreness
Sudden numbness or weakness in arms or legs
Chest pain or heavy pressure in the chest during exercise
Dizziness, loss of balance, or blurred vision while training
Shortness of breath disproportionate to exercise intensity
→ See a doctor before resuming training

pillarE.prevention_subtitle: Prevention beats cure — build small habits daily
warning_signs: Sharp, sudden pain (not normal muscle soreness)
Sudden numbness or muscle weakness in arms/legs
Chest pain or heavy pressure during exercise
Dizziness, loss of balance, blurred vision
Shortness of breath disproportionate to effort
prevention_habits: Eat diversely, enough micronutrients, less processed food
Sleep 7–9h/night — poor sleep increases chronic disease risk
Manage stress: meditation, training, social connection
Annual health check-up once per year

pillarF.title: Tools & Resources
pillarF.subtitle: Tools
pillarF.description: Checklists, templates, and progress tests to track your healthy journey.

sections.title: Daily Checklist
items: 10–20 minutes of movement (training, walking, stretching)
2 handfuls of vegetables per meal — fresh, varied
1 protein source per main meal — meat, fish, eggs, tofu
Drink 1.5–2 liters of water
Sleep 7–8 hours, in bed before 11 PM
5 minutes of breathing or meditation — any time of day
No phone for 30 minutes before sleep

sections.title: Weekly Checklist
items: Complete 3–5 planned training sessions
Prepare food for the week (meal prep 1–2 hours on weekends)
Check progress: weight, waist measurement, overall feeling
Schedule next week's sessions — confirm specific days/times
Spend 1 hour on a relaxing activity you enjoy (reading, walking)

sections.title: Templates
items: Training journal: date · exercise · sets · reps · how it felt
7-day meal plan: breakfast/lunch/dinner + snacks
15-min morning routine: water · sunlight · movement · meditation
20-min evening routine: shower · reading/journaling · no screens

sections.title: 4-Week Progress Test
items: Endurance test: 6-minute fast walk — measure distance covered
Strength test: max push-ups + max squats in 1 set
Flexibility test: standing straight, can you touch the floor?
Measure waist and body weight (morning, before eating)
Record results and compare at week 4, 8, and 12

sections.title: Training Log (5 Questions After Each Session)
items: 1. What exercises did I do today? (brief list)
2. How many minutes?
3. Perceived exertion RPE 1–10?
4. Any unusual pain or discomfort?
5. Next session: increase reps, sets, difficulty, or maintain?
